citation_changes.quote: Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ and $N\ge1$ be integers. Let $Q_d=\mathbb R^d/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^d$ carry the probability measure obtained by pushing normalized Haar measure on $\mathbb T^d=\mathbb R^d/\mathbb Z^d$ forward under $y\mapsto x=2\pi y$; in coordinates this is $(2\pi)^{-d}dx$. For any componentwise integrable real $q:Q_d\to\mathbb R^N$, considered up to equality almost everywhere, and $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, define its componentwise Fourier coefficient by $\widehat q(k)=\int_{Q_d}q(x)e^{-ik\cdot x}\,d\mu(x)$; this integral is finite because $|e^{ik\cdot x}|=1$ and $q\in L^1$. A finite real trigonometric polynomial is a finite sum $q(x)=\sum_{k\in F}a_ke^{ik\cdot x}$, where $F\subset\mathbb Z^d$ is finite and the coefficients, extended by zero outside $F$, satisfy $a_{-k}=\overline{a_k}$. Such polynomials are integrable and satisfy $\widehat q(-k)=\overline{\widehat q(k)}$. Put $w_k=(1+|k|^2)^{1/2}$. For any $s\in\mathbb R$, define $H^s(Q_d;\mathbb R^N)$ as the completion of finite real trigonometric polynomials in the norm $\|q\|_{H^s}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}w_k^{2s}|\widehat q(k)|^2$. Identify this completion with the weighted coefficient space subject to conjugate symmetry, using finite symmetric cutoffs, and write $\widehat q(k)$ for its coefficient coordinate. If $s\ge0$, each element has a unique $L^2$ representative, and its coefficient coordinate agrees with the normalized integral formula; for $s<0$ no $L^2$ representative is asserted.

derivation_changes.claim:
For each scalar component $f$ of the smooth initial data and every integer $N\ge0$, periodic integration by parts gives $(1+|k|^2)^N\widehat f(k)=\widehat{(1-\Delta)^Nf}(k)$, where $\Delta=\sum_{j=1}^d\partial_{x_j}^2$; opposite periodic-face terms cancel. Since $(1-\Delta)^Nf$ is continuous on the compact torus, its $L^1$ norm $C_{f,N}$ is finite, and $|\widehat f(k)|\le C_{f,N}(1+|k|^2)^{-N}$.
For any integer $m\ge0$, choose $N$ with $4N-2m>d$. The shell $j\le|k|<j+1$ contains at most $C_d(j+1)^{d-1}$ lattice points, by placing disjoint unit cubes at its lattice points inside a shell of fixed enlarged width, so $\sum_k(1+|k|^2)^{m-2N}<\infty$ by comparison with $\sum_{j\ge1}j^{d-1+2m-4N}$. Thus every initial component belongs to every $H^m$ under [F1].
Multiplying the mode identity $E_k(t)=E_k(0)$ from step 2.1 by $(1+|k|^2)^m$ and summing these nonnegative finite-energy series proves, by [F2], the stated conserved weighted energy. In particular both coefficient families remain in every $H^m$, uniformly for all real time.
